description: Pebbled black under a net of branching cyan that will not sit still. Warm. Its spark rarely stops at one body.
lore: The register the graders keep has two columns that do not mean the same thing: the ground a stone came off, and the nature it turns out to have. Black rock, fire. High snow, frost. The columns are two ways of saying one thing, and in every line but this one they agree. This comes down off the high snow — a great many days uphill, on the wrong side of the massif entirely from the ground where the emptying is supposed to happen — and it grades storm, on evidence a child could check, which is that it throws a spark. It is also worth more than anything else that comes off that mountain, and only some of that is the walk.

Set it on a table between the two stones it ought to resemble, the pale blue rimed one and the grey one with the single cyan seam. Those two are cold to the hand whatever they are underneath; you put them down colder than you picked them up. This one has nothing cold on it at all. It is pebbled black, netted all through the gaps between the pebbles with cyan, near-white down the middle of each line and going teal at the edges, branching and then branching again off the branches, and it is warm the whole way out to the surface. The stone-workers make a good deal of that. The people who work the high snow make nothing of it and are not being difficult: every hard piece is warm underneath, and how far the warmth gets has never settled an argument. The light settles nothing either. Watch the net a while and it has gone somewhere else in it, and then somewhere else again, and it has not once been seen to stop.

Setting one is the part the smiths talk about, because it will not stay inside its own outline. Put it to an edge and by the time the setting is finished the light is in the metal as well, and the first thing anyone learns fighting with one is not to let a friend stand at their shoulder. The spark goes where it was sent, and then now and again it is not there any more; it is in the next body along, whichever body that happens to be. That is the entire disagreement in one object and neither side has given ground. Cold at that height is not a temperature, say the ones who live in it, it is a thing that comes and gets you the moment the glove is off, and a storm is only what that amounts to when there is enough of it. A hard piece is the last of what a creature was, say the ones who grade them, and that creature was the colour and the temperature of the mountain from the crest of its head down to its claws, and cold does not go looking. What can be said without taking a side is that everything you can learn standing in front of one of those says hunger, and hunger is not a direction. This is the only thing ever to come off one that says which way.
